12:45 Local Time, 07:15 GMT, 12:45 IST: With the 2027 ODI World Cup now less than a year away, every series from here on will inevitably be viewed through the lens of the showpiece event in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. For India, where the spotlight is rarely dim, every performance will bring its share of interest, praise and scrutiny. Hello and welcome, everyone! It’s time for the first ODI between India and West Indies in Thiruvananthapuram.

On paper, it is a contest between the No.1 and No.10 teams in the ODI rankings. WI’s record vs India makes for difficult reading. They have not won an ODI series in India since 2002, while their last series win against India came in 2006. Since then, they have lost 13 consecutive ODI series against the Men in Blue. West Indies will also have a longer road to the 2027 World Cup, with their place in the tournament to be decided through the Qualifiers. Shai Hope and his men have their work cut out. But India are hardly entering this series without questions of their own, having lost two of their last three ODI series. So, can WI spring a surprise, or will India have it their way once again?

Aadya Sharma is at the venue nice and early, and he has some updates for us: "Good afternoon from Trivandrum. Just managed to get in, there's a sea of blue outside, and a great number of Rohit fans posing in front of his massive cutout. There are enough Kohli jerseys to match that, with the obvious Samson representation, and a few Dhonis, Pandyas and Tendulkars sprinkled around. The skies are completely clear, barring a very thin scattering of clouds on one side. It rained briefly on Friday evening, but it was all clear on Saturday, and it's baking hot right now."

He adds: "Both teams have arrived at the ground. Virat Kohli walks out with a bat in hand to massive cheers, and is currently taking throwdowns on one side. Gautam Gambhir is chatting with his old teammate Irfan Pathan as both Shubman Gill and Daren Sammy (WI head coach)take a reading of the pitch There's a small strapping on Gill's right elbow, in the region where he was hit in the nets on Friday." Yes, that’s right. Gill was hit on the elbow by a Mohammed Siraj delivery during a practice session and needed plenty of icing afterwards. But the good news is that he seems match-ready.

Not everything is smooth sailing for India in this format. Since winning the Champions Trophy in 2025, India have played five ODI series and lost three of them. They will also be without Shreyas Iyer, Axar Patel and Jasprit Bumrah, all currently in Japan for the Asian Games, while their star all-rounder Hardik Pandya is sidelined with an injury. Their absences open the door for Ruturaj Gaikwad, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Ravindra Jadeja to strengthen their case. In Bumrah’s absence, India’s pace attack will also be under the microscope. Prasidh Krishna and Gurnoor Brar have struggled for consistency, while Mohammed Siraj has played just nine ODIs since the 2023 World Cup, taking only eight wickets at 46.87. The current management also values batting depth at No. 8, so don’t be surprised if Auqib Nabi gets an opportunity at some point in the series.
